A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoGuide work, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. Retained material can be matched, including v1 Appendix D becoming v2 Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original HouseExpo reconstruction experiments, intersection-penalty and optimizer ablations, measurement-noise tests, and posterior-sampling analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds CFG+CoGuide results, measurements from two apartments, a CFG guidance sweep, and audio-restoration results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds CFG+CoGuide, replacing the unconditional diffusion prior with a trajectory-conditioned CFG model. Appendix D adds an audio adaptation using a shared CQT-based CNN/ResNet encoder and continuous-time contrastive guidance. These extend the procedure substantially while retaining the original floorplan method.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic HouseExpo trajectories, v2 evaluates UWB-measured human trajectories from two apartments. Appendix D introduces piano-audio restoration, with MAESTRO training data and degraded recordings, substantially extending both input conditions and task coverage.

E2.justification: The six original floorplan baselines remain unchanged. The new audio comparison evaluates LTAS equalization and an unprocessed-recording control against CoGuide (Table 4). BABE2 is discussed but is not an evaluated comparator in that table.

E3.justification: The original 64×64 HouseExpo setup, 80/10/10 split, and F1/IoU metrics remain. New protocols include UWB trajectory acquisition and projection, 22,050-Hz audio with 8.35-second crops, FAD evaluation using VGG/PANN, and RMSE/MAE-based CFG tuning. Newly disclosed CFG training settings do not establish changes to earlier runs.

E4.justification: v2 adds a CFG guidance-scale sensitivity plot (Appendix C.2), a conditional-prior comparison through CFG+CoGuide, and two qualitative cases examining synthetic-to-real generalization. These are bounded additions; the existing intersection-weight, optimizer, noise, embedding, uncertainty, and planner analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The original floorplan tables retain mean±standard-deviation reporting, and Appendix B retains distance-transform variance across five seeds. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is introduced. The added audio table reports point estimates only.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores and Tables 2–3 are unchanged. The added CFG+CoGuide row reports sparse/moderate/dense F1 of 0.93/0.97/0.99 and IoU of 0.87/0.93/0.97. New apartment reconstructions, guidance-sweep results, and audio results substantially expand the evidence. Table 4 reports FAD-VGG 0.84 versus LTAS 2.88 and scaled FAD-PANN 0.19 versus 0.27.

T1.justification: The central InfoNCE likelihood-ratio argument and Appendix A derivation remain unchanged. Appendix D adds a limited formal extension through the audio probability-flow ODE and contrastive posterior update. Algorithm 1 also inserts the previously missing gradient on the intersection-penalty term.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims floorplan reconstruction and presents blind inverse problems as future work. v2 reframes the abstract around a broader class of partially specified, nonsmooth operators and claims demonstrated applicability beyond spatial mapping through blind audio restoration; the introduction and conclusion adopt this broader contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly attributes CFG’s real-world failures to the shift from synthetic A* trajectories to sparse human trajectories. v2 also explains conditional-prior complementarity and defines its audio setting as requiring neither an analytical degradation operator nor operator estimation at inference. Existing furniture and ill-posedness discussions remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies substantial CFG architecture/training details, audio preprocessing and encoder hyperparameters, and UWB collection procedures. It newly states that all baselines receive the intersection penalty and that DiPPeR was reimplemented because official code was unavailable; these disclosures do not establish changed implementations. Direct DiffPIR/DMPlug URLs are removed, while the project access statement remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds audio-restoration, MAESTRO, FAD, CQT, and UWB references, and contrasts its audio guidance with Moliner et al.’s operator-estimation approach. CFG attribution changes to Ho and Salimans, and related work adds Amballa et al. The established floorplan research positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, local grammar and terminology are edited, and new experimental and implementation subsections are inserted. Conference headers, acknowledgments, and the conclusion heading change. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds apartment comparisons (Figure 5), a CFG sweep (Figure 10), audio spectrograms (Figure 11), and the FAD table. Table 1 gains a hybrid-method row and moves; Figure 4 is redrawn. Existing qualitative, uncertainty, retrieval, and planner images are retained and renumbered, with planner figures placed beside their discussions.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1’s exclusively synthetic empirical foundation through measured apartment trajectories and a worked audio-restoration application, while documenting the important CFG baseline and testing its integration with CoGuide. These additions address significant validation and reproducibility gaps. The gains remain qualified: apartment evidence is limited to two qualitative cases, audio evaluation lacks a clear test-set size, and Figure 10 does not display the stated selected guidance scale of 1.5.
